races.name: goracing.co.uk Future Stars Apprentice Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Tarlac
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer in form but forced away from its natural rearward berth in this field; its best recent effort is a second over course and trip on Good ground (22 days ago), and the trainer sends a single runner rather than a team, so any run close to that form is its ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Tarlac has run over today's trip and going before, and that placed effort last time out offers mild encouragement, though he's winless in his last six starts and a mid-field ranking here suggests he faces a stiff task converting promise into something more tangible.

runners_data.name: Thank The Lord
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old wearing a visor and returning after 105 days off, with the trainer reporting 0 winners from 5 runners in the past fortnight; best form came on Standard surfaces rather than turf Good, and the lengthy absence alongside the hold-up style compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 105 days off, Thank The Lord faces a stiff task on these figures — ranked seventh of nine — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and draw two offers a handy pitch from which to find early cover.

runners_data.name: Tickets
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied hold-up type with a tidy placed record at this trip, including a win over 6f; jockey Harry Vigors claims 3lb which helps compensate for an OR of 48, and the 42-day break is not alarming given the horse's consistency in similar classified company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Tickets nonetheless showed ability with a second last time out and a second five starts back — yet fifth-place finishes in between suggest inconsistency. Fit enough at 42 days, he has distance and going experience, though the 135 lb burden is a concern.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent recent form, with two placed efforts from seven runs at the 6f Good combination and a career-best effort just 16 days ago; Conor Whiteley is a capable booking and the trainer's 2-from-16 strike rate over 14 days reflects a yard sending horses fit rather than cold.
runners_data.comment: Mister Sky Blue shaped with promise when second four starts back and arrives here fit off a 16-day break, with experience over today's trip and going and our rating of 58 pointing to unexploited potential; the risk is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Mrs Trump
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with the most turf-Good experience in the race (12 from 15 runs), including two wins at the trip, but those victories have dried up recently and the short 9-day turnaround from a seventh of eight needs factoring in alongside a trainer who has not fired in 25 recent runners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mrs Trump faces a stiff task here — a sequence of mid-division finishes and a trainer yet to strike in 23 recent attempts make her hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Newyorkstateofmind
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old blinker-wearer whose natural style is to come from the back; held forward of its ideal position in the map because the rear is congested, and its recent form of 0-2-6-8-4 on Good ground suggests it lacks the finishing kick to make up ground from a compromised pitch.
runners_data.comment: Newyorkstateofmind heads into this off a 32-day break with distance and going experience to call on, and our rating of 58 marks him out as the one to beat in this field. Winless in his last six starts, but that fourth two runs back hints at residual ability worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Drish Samphire
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a material concern over 6f on a flat, galloping track; true hold-up style is further displaced forward on this map, and its 0-from-9 record on Good-going surfaces adds to the case against.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Drish Samphire has shown little encouragement with finishes of sixth, sixth, seventh and eighth in recent outings, and ranked last on our figures here, she's hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going, and a quick turnaround keeping her fresh.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: The race's lone pace-setter and tactically pivotal: seven-year-old with a formidable record on Good ground (12/15 runs, 2 wins, 5 places) and has placed three times in five at this trip; the STYLE_FIT tag flags it is asked to lead in a field where it may face slight pressure early, but no rival has the profile to sustain a serious challenge from the front.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last four starts, Golden Prosperity arrives here in sharp order just nine days after his latest run, has experience over today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 55 puts him 6lb above his official rating of 49; the concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with Good-ground course form (11/15 runs at this trip) and a second over C&D recently; nine-year-old trained by Peter Niven has not won in recent memory but rarely runs badly, and Ethan Tindall's booking keeps costs manageable at 135lbs.
runners_data.comment: Hurstwood has run over today's trip and going before and ran a solid fourth last time out, just 20 days ago, so fitness isn't a concern — yet he remains winless in recent starts, and that lack of a breakthrough is the obvious question mark against him here.

races.paceDynamic: Golden Prosperity is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine pace-setter to push against, should be able to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated gallop from the off. Mister Sky Blue and Hurstwood offer nominal prominent support but neither is likely to force the issue, meaning Golden Prosperity can dictate every fraction on this flat 6f track. The bulk of the field — Tarlac, Drish Samphire, and Newyorkstateofmind — are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed, so they will not be racing in their most potent positions. A controlled, honest pace on good ground over 6f at Thirsk strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, making prominent-to-lead profiles the clear tactical beneficiaries; hold-up horses denied their natural rear position face an uphill task to manufacture a winning run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Golden Prosperity Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity is allowed a soft lead and controls the tempo throughout without any rival applying pressure.
scenarios.body: Golden Prosperity dictates from the front, setting a comfortable pace that neither burns off the prominent horses nor allows the hold-up brigade to build momentum behind; in a compressed, even gallop the horse at the head of affairs retains maximum energy for the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit Front Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Sky Blue or Hurstwood track Golden Prosperity closely and overhaul it in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A pace just honest enough to string the field out allows the closest pursuers to peg back Golden Prosperity as it tires inside the final furlong; both Mister Sky Blue and Hurstwood have shown consistent placing form at this trip on good ground and are best positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front-runners tie each other up, creating a fast-run race that sets up a late run.
scenarios.body: Tarlac and Newyorkstateofmind, though forced forward of their ideal pitch, still carry hold-up profiles and could benefit if a rare fast gallop opens the back straight up; however, the redistribution of multiple hold-up types means none will be tracking from a true rearward position, blunting the impact of any late swoop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Start Scrambles Shape
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners break sharply and fight for prominent positions, creating a chaotic early pace that unsettles Golden Prosperity's rhythm.
scenarios.body: A scrappy pace battle in the opening two furlongs would expose Golden Prosperity if its rhythm is broken, handing an opportunity to whichever hold-up horse finds the clearest passage widest; Drish Samphire's tendency to fade in the finish makes this scenario unlikely to suit it, while Mrs Trump, with the most Good-ground experience in the field, might sneak a minor prize.

watchPoints.text: Golden Prosperity's early stride — if it meets any resistance from Mister Sky Blue or Hurstwood in the first furlong, its ability to control tempo is undermined and the race shape shifts entirely.

Tarlac's position at the start — watch whether Olivia Haines (3lb claimer) attempts to settle the horse off the pace or is forced to race prominently; any scramble for position will see this horse racing well outside its comfort zone.

Thank The Lord returning after 105 days — horses trained by W H Harrison off a long break have a poor recent strike rate, and the visor may not compensate for a lack of race fitness against rivals who are sharp.

Drish Samphire drawn and positioned to feature early, but the fade-in-finish flag means it is worth monitoring how quickly it drops away in the closing stages, which could block ground for hold-up runners coming from midfield.
Trainer Ruth Carr has sent Newyorkstateofmind out five times in 27 days — watch the market for any drift that signals the horse is there for fitness rather than a win bid.

races.name: Bob Vickery Memorial Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Peter Bell Memorial Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bymiddaytomorrow
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with a 7f Good win on her most recent start; Ed Walker's filly steps forward on that evidence but races here from a prominent/lead style that is slightly out of her natural rhythm per the style-fit flag, which moderates her win claims even if she controls the pace.
runners_data.comment: Bymiddaytomorrow comes here on the back of a win last time out and a trainer firing at 26% in the last fortnight — a potent combination. She has run over today's trip before, carries 141 lb from stall one, and our rating puts her clear at the head of this six-runner field.

runners_data.name: Gerry's Darling
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's filly arrives with consecutive wins, the latest over 7f on Good ground matching today's conditions precisely, and Kevin Stott takes over in the saddle; four runs on similar going yielding a win and two places makes her the standout profile for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Gerry's Darling arrives in cracking nick — a winner last time out and second two starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions. Carrying 134 lb from stall 5 is the concern, but her recent form makes her a serious threat.

runners_data.name: Love Tanya
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's filly is a genuine hold-up type whose two runs have both produced places over the exact trip and going combination she faces today; Oisin Orr is an upgrade in class and she is the hold-up horse most likely to get her natural position at the back given the redistribution of Bonjour Belle and Spirit of Mary.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last two starts, Love Tanya arrives here on a sharp 14-day turnaround with distance experience in her favour — a consistent threat despite being yet to win. The main risk is that our rating of 64 leaves her with something to find against the top-rated runners.

runners_data.name: Consultation
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's filly has only placed at 6f so far and today's step up to 7f on Good ground is the key question after 42 days off; if she takes to the extra furlong she could be competitive racing prominently, but her form figures are modest and the lay-off is a flag.

runners_data.name: Bonjour Belle
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's filly has form figures of 10-7-5, struggling to land a blow in nurseries; her true instinct is to race at the rear but the crowded hold-up group means she will likely be pushed further forward than ideal, compromising her chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Bonjour Belle heads here having finished no better than fifth in recent outings, and while she has run over today's trip before, it's hard to make a case at these weights against stronger-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Priscilla's Hope
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer for Philip McBride with a placed run at 6f Good but no wins from five starts; steps up to 7f for the first time today, and while the extra furlong may suit, Andrew Mullen will need the pace scenario to play into her hands from a wide draw.
runners_data.comment: Priscilla's Hope has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 64 puts her clear of her official mark — a solid case for improvement, though she remains winless in her last five starts and that consistency concern is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Spirit of Mary
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's filly has three placed efforts over 6f on Good ground but sits lowest in the weights at OR 45 and has been repositioned on the map away from her natural rear berth; Ethan Tindall (5) is a claim booking but the combination of lowest rating, redistribution displacement, and no win from five starts makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Spirit of Mary nevertheless shows some consistency with thirds in her two most recent outings, and she has run over today's trip and going before; drawn in stall two and carrying 114 lb, she faces a stiff task on our figures as the lowest-rated runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Bymiddaytomorrow is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with only Gerry's Darling and Consultation as genuine prominent challengers in a seven-runner field, she should be able to bowl along at a controlled, self-set tempo over Thirsk's flat seven furlongs without being seriously pressured for the lead. Gerry's Darling arrives on the back of back-to-back wins including a 7f Good success and is the most likely horse to sit just off Bymiddaytomorrow's shoulder, meaning the pace will be honest but not brutal — a recipe for a steadily-run affair that favours those who can travel prominently and finish off. The hold-up contingent — Love Tanya, Bonjour Belle, Priscilla's Hope and Spirit of Mary — are all coming from the back, but Bonjour Belle and Spirit of Mary are genuine closers who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded; neither is likely to secure their natural position, making true late-run scenarios less potent than they appear. This race shape — a lone leader under a sustainable gallop, a prominent chaser close by, and a bunched hold-up group — strongly favours horses who can race handily near the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, giving the prominent and front-running profiles a clear structural edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bymiddaytomorrow dictates a measured tempo and the prominent horses travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Bymiddaytomorrow sets a fair but unhurried pace and Gerry's Darling, cruising just off the shoulder, swoops past inside the final furlong with her proven 7f/Good form translating directly; Consultation may also find the conditions and trip suiting her better than her 6f nursery runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Bymiddaytomorrow is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the gallop is slow enough that she steals first run entering the straight.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to challenge her early, Bymiddaytomorrow can conserve energy and produce a strong finishing effort herself on this step up to 7f where she already has a win; the prominent trackers fail to close the gap in time on ground that rewards relaxed front-runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front-running and prominent types tie each other up, leaving a gap for a closer.
scenarios.body: Love Tanya is the most credible beneficiary given her genuine hold-up profile and consistent placed form over 7f on Good ground with Oisin Orr aboard; Priscilla's Hope would need things to go very right from the rear but cannot be entirely dismissed on her best form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If a messy early tempo creates a bunched field and the race is decided by a sprint finish in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up types converging at once and the prominent horses unable to build a meaningful advantage, any of the midfield runners could get involved in a tight photo; Bonjour Belle and Spirit of Mary are the least likely to truly benefit here given they are displaced from their natural rear position and lack the proven form to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Gerry's Darling — her 7f Good profile maps perfectly onto today's race shape; if Kevin Stott slots her just off Bymiddaytomorrow's shoulder she could be travelling ominously well turning for home and is the horse most likely to dictate the finish.

Bymiddaytomorrow — watch whether she is allowed to bowl along uncontested or whether Gerry's Darling and Consultation apply enough early pressure to compromise her stamina reserve over the extra furlong she has only won over once.

Love Tanya — as the only hold-up horse not redistributed on the map, she has a clear run at the back-marker position; if Oisin Orr positions her smartly and the pace is genuine, she is the main threat to the prominent pair in the straight.

Consultation — 42 days off and a step up in trip both need to be taken on trust; watch her in the paddock and early in the race to see whether she settles and travels, as a prominent horse who is ring-rusty could find herself exposed turning for home.

Bonjour Belle and Spirit of Mary — both true closers displaced into the midfield by the congested hold-up group; if neither can drop back to find cover early, they may race too keenly and weaken rather than finish, narrowing the competitive field in the home straight.

races.name: Ladies' Day Saturday 5th September - Book Now Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Qila
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Brian Ellison returning after 59 days off; best recent form came on Soft/Standard going and the step back to Good turf here needs respecting, though the 5f trip suits — will need the race to develop in her favour from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Qila is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip before and a second two starts back offers a crumb of form; 59 days off and 130 lb to carry add to the questions.

runners_data.name: Glory Fighter
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's veteran ten-year-old has a solid recent win on Good at 5f but is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rearward position is cramped in a six-runner field; the field is denser at the back than the pace map suggests, making a clear late run harder to find.
runners_data.comment: Glory Fighter has finished sixth and unplaced in his last two starts, and with his trainer yet to strike from 23 runners in the past fortnight, it's hard to make a case — despite experience over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's four-year-old arrives in sharp form (two wins in last five, ran 10 days ago) and is a natural front-runner or prominent racer who, in a field already boasting J Street, will likely be squeezed into a tracking role rather than leading — how well they adapt to sitting second or third rather than bowling along up front is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Azuinthejungle arrives in cracking nick — a winner two starts back and again last time out, fit on just a 10-day turnaround, and with experience of today's trip and conditions. The main risk is that he's up against the top-rated runner in a field of six.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has been posting mediocre form figures (7th, 9th, 17th recent runs) on similar Good ground at the same trip, and while the tongue-strap is noted, the consistent lack of impact in handicaps at this mark is a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of six in the field on our figures, Vince L'Amour has run over today's trip and going and arrives fresh on 13 days' rest — yet winless in his last six starts, and a trainer in poor current form at 2/83 is the key concern.

runners_data.name: J Street
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's four-year-old is the lone confirmed pace-setter and, with Billy Garritty able to dictate unchallenged, will set the terms for the entire race — won last twice at 5f and holds a favourable tactical position, though the STYLE_FIT tag hints this may not be a perfectly clean role given field dynamics.
runners_data.comment: J Street won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with a 13-day turnaround suggesting she arrives fresh and ready; at 135 lb from stall one, the weight burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Military Girl
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners a horse in strong recent form — three wins from last five, all at 5f on Good or similar ground — and a prominent, forward-going style suits this race shape perfectly; the 52-day break is the only minor query, but Michael Dods conditions horses to arrive fit.
runners_data.comment: Military Girl arrives here in fine fettle, a winner twice in her last five starts including back-to-back victories, and she shaped well with a second last time out. She has run over today's trip and going, and a 52-day break shouldn't blunt her edge.

races.paceDynamic: J Street is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press them from the gate on a flat 5f at Thirsk, Billy Garritty can dictate a controlled, honest gallop without being harassed. Military Girl and Azuinthejungle are the natural prominent types who will push to track J Street closely in the first two furlongs, creating a genuine but not frantic early tempo. Qila, Vince L'Amour, and the redistributed Glory Fighter will be operating from further back, though Glory Fighter's true hold-up profile means ground will need to be made up from a disadvantaged position in a small six-runner field where the gaps may not materialise late. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a fair, metronomic pace on Good turf — strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the leader and pounce in the final furlong, rather than true closers who need the front to tie up; this field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, with Glory Fighter and Qila both genuine off-the-pace runners who will struggle to get a true waiting position given the modest field size.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: J Street Controls, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If J Street secures an uncontested lead and Military Girl or Azuinthejungle sit smoothly just off the pace before sprinting clear.
scenarios.body: J Street rolls along at a fair but manageable gallop, leaving the prominent duo ideally poised turning for home on the flat Thirsk straight; the horse with the best finishing kick from second or third position wins this comfortably.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Bowls Over All
scenarios.trigger: If J Street's uncontested lead allows the gallop to become so comfortable that they simply quicken away from the field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no pressure and a confident Garritty ride, J Street never truly comes off the bridle and the race is over before the hold-up horses can get competitive; a wire-to-wire success at a fair price.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the front rank tie up inside the final furlong, giving the hold-up horses a clear run through.
scenarios.body: Qila and Glory Fighter would need a fast-run race where J Street and the prominent pair have emptied their tanks, allowing a sweeping late run — possible but dependent on a pace shape this field is unlikely to produce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If Military Girl or Azuinthejungle challenges J Street hard from the gate, turning this into a genuine pace battle.
scenarios.body: A hot early fraction burns off the front runners before halfway, reshuffling the race completely and opening it up for any horse who has been nursed into the race; chaotic shape, low probability given J Street's clear pace advantage.

watchPoints.text: Military Girl has hit the board in four of her last five on Good 5f ground and arrives in the exact tactical position this race shape favours — watch her as the prime beneficiary if J Street sets a fair, uncontested pace.

Azuinthejungle's natural front-running instinct may lead to an early speed duel with J Street if connections push for the lead; if that happens, both horses could be vulnerable late having burned too much energy in the opening two furlongs.

Glory Fighter is a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield map position — in a six-runner race with limited gaps, watch whether David Nolan can find a clear passage in the straight or whether the horse is continually hampered by the compressed field.

Vince L'Amour's recent form figures at this trip and going are poor (7th, 9th, 17th) and the tongue-strap has not sparked a revival yet — watch the market for any unusual support that might suggest a stable confidence signal before dismissing entirely.

J Street's last two wins at 5f make the front-running scenario credible, but Billy Garritty will need to judge the pace carefully — if he goes too slow, prominent rivals pounce; if he goes too fast under pressure, closers threaten late.

races.name: William Hill, Market Place, Thirsk Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Master Vintner
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's progressive 4yo has won and placed over 12f on Standard but steps up to 1m4f here on good turf; as the sole natural front-runner he controls the tactical framing, though the STYLE_FIT tag indicates he is racing slightly out of his most comfortable role and his flat-track Chelmsford form may not fully translate.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive runner-up finishes on his two most recent starts paint Master Vintner as a horse in excellent heart, and a winner five starts back underlines his ability. He has run over today's distance and going, and 36 days off shouldn't blunt his edge carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley rides this 8yo hold-up horse who has placed twice from 15 runs at roughly similar going conditions; his best recent effort was a 2nd over 12f on good and the step up to 1m4f on the Thirsk flat gives him a legitimate chance, but he needs the pace to lift.
runners_data.comment: Majestic was second two starts back, and he has run over today's distance and going before — at 132 lb he carries plenty of weight, which is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo runs freshly off a 13-day turnaround and is fitted with a hood; a genuine hold-up type whose best good-ground run (3rd over 12f) came at a longer trip, he needs more pace than this race is likely to generate, and the minimum 10f history suggests 1m4f is at the outer edge of his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Wahdan steps back up looking for a first win in recent starts, but he's shown enough with a third last time out and has run over today's trip and going — his rating of 97 tops this field. The worry is a trainer in the depths of a lean spell at just 2%.

runners_data.name: Sudu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 4yo returns from a 373-day absence, which is the dominant concern here — that layoff introduces significant unknown fitness risk despite a striking win over 12f on good last time out; if cherry-fit he has the profile to sit prominently and threaten, but the absence makes form assessment speculative.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 373 days makes Sudu very hard to trust on return, and eighth last time out does him no favours; he has run over today's trip and going, and the trainer's 37% strike rate over 14 days offers a rare crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4yo has posted consistent placed efforts (three times 3rd or 4th) and appears an unknown quantity for style given the U tag; at OR 83 he is the least exposed in terms of upside and Andrew Mullen may look to track the pace, with the 1m4f trip on good a feasible profile match based on his 12f placed run.
runners_data.comment: Wanderlust showed a return to form with a win four starts back and was placed third last time out, and his going experience is a clear asset at 127 lb; the concern is a 43-day absence that leaves his sharpness open to question.

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: A genuine deep hold-up horse who has been pushed onto the midfield map position because the field is heavy with closers; Tim Easterby's 5yo showed ability with a 2nd at 11f on good but needs a truly-run race to make ground, and the STYLE_FIT tag is a meaningful caution against overstating his chance in a shape that will likely be run at a measured tempo.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a tame ninth last time out, Golden West is a tough one to fancy at the foot of our rankings — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and at least returns here fresh enough at 28 days since his last run.

races.paceDynamic: Master Vintner is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only five rivals, faces no realistic threat for the early lead over this 1m4f trip at Thirsk. Sudu is also mapped prominent but is returning from 373 days off and is unlikely to apply sustained pressure, leaving Master Vintner free to control tempo at a measured, sustainable gallop. The race will unfold with Master Vintner bowling along comfortably in front, a small bunch tracking through the middle, and the hold-up trio — Majestic, Wahdan, and true hold-up type Golden West — needing a meaningful injection of pace in the home straight to close. Note that Golden West is a genuine deep hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map because the field carries more hold-up types than can all sit at the rear; Golden West is most likely to actually settle furthest back, with Majestic and Wahdan the ones who may acquire a more prominent berth than usual. This race shape strongly favours the horse travelling prominently or pressing the leader, as the pace is unlikely to be fierce enough to gift closers a winning gap unless something goes wrong up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vintner Controls, Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If Master Vintner dictates an uncontested, honest pace and the hold-up horses find the tempo insufficient to close.
scenarios.body: Master Vintner sets a controlled fractions, the field strings out on the turn into the home straight, and any closer lacks the lead-change stimulus to land a telling blow; the prominent tracking position becomes the race-winning berth.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Presser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Master Vintner sets a true, honest gallop and a prominent tracker times a late challenge perfectly.
scenarios.body: A steady but genuine pace means one of the horses sitting just off the leader — Sudu or Wanderlust — travels sweetly before delivering a challenge in the final two furlongs; this shape rewards the horse with the best turn of foot from close range.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Master Vintner goes too hard early or the race develops a strongly-run middle sector that backs the field up.
scenarios.body: A genuinely-run race drains the front-runners' reserves, opening the door for Majestic or Wahdan to pick up ground through the final furlong on the soft side of good; Majestic's two-placed runs at this kind of trip on good ground make him the most credible beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Falls Away
scenarios.trigger: If Master Vintner is taken on unexpectedly or weakens badly in the final quarter-mile after setting a fast pace.
scenarios.body: A scrambled or collapse scenario gifts the race to whoever has been ridden quietly and delivers the most sustained late effort; Golden West, though a true hold-up type shuffled to midfield on the map, possesses the course form to capitalise but is dependent on genuine pace collapse.

watchPoints.text: Master Vintner's unchallenged lead — if no horse pressures him through the first mile, watch whether Greatrex allows fractions to drop to a crawl that turns this into a sprint finish, neutralising hold-up horses entirely.
Sudu's fitness — Roger Varian runners returning from 373 days off can be sharper than expected but also need the run; watch the market move in the final 30 minutes as a guide to stable confidence.

Golden West's true running position — mapped to midfield but a natural backmarker; if Fentiman pushes forward early to avoid being shuffled back, it signals this race shape is messier than the settled pace map suggests.

Wahdan's hood — the headgear flags a potential temperament or keenness factor for Tim Easterby's hold-up horse; if he races freely in the first mile he will not be running his race in the final furlong.

Wanderlust's first-run tactics — with an unknown U style tag, watch how Mullen positions out of the gates; if he tracks Master Vintner prominently, this represents a meaningful upgrade from the mid-division profile and makes the horse a more serious player in Scenario B.

races.name: Country Music Night Here Next Friday 14th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hellcat
runners_data.note: A genuine come-from-behind type trained by Ross Burdon whose best efforts have come when able to produce a late run, but with several true hold-up horses in this field, they will find it harder to drop out and get the race they want; five from eight on similar going but no wins or places on Good in recent runs, and the 31-day absence adds a small query.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Hellcat faces a stiff ask here; the third three starts back is a flicker of ability, and she has run over today's trip and going, but the overall profile makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3yo has solid claims on a pace-shape read — prominent-style runner, winner on Soft and placed multiple times on Good, and David Allan's booking for a yard in strong recent form (T14: 3/82) adds confidence; the step back from 7-8f trips to 6f is the key query, but early speed suits.
runners_data.comment: Lope Y Linda was a winner four starts back and arrives here on a quick 16-day turnaround with distance and going experience in her favour, but consecutive fourths in her last two runs and a trainer in poor form (2%) are real concerns at 124 lb from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Liquid Cooled
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's 3yo has a win on Standfast ground and placed at 6f on Good, and Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) keeps costs down; naturally a hold-up horse by profile, though the number of closers in the field means they will likely race closer to the pace than ideal, blunting their typical finish.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Liquid Cooled has disappointed in his last three starts — fifth most recently — and rates hard to fancy at the weights, though he has run over today's trip before and the 21-day break at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Agric Ranger
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's second runner here has finished in the 4-7 range across five recent starts and has yet to place on Good ground in their history (0W0P on similar); naturally races from off the pace but will struggle to get back in a moderately-paced race, and Duran Fentiman has limited material to work with.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Agric Ranger faces a stiff ask here — a trainer striking at just 2% in the last 14 days does little to encourage confidence, though he has run over today's trip before and goes from stall three.

runners_data.name: Overbudget
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3yo carries the highest weight of the prominent types (133lbs, OR 63) and has placed twice including a third at 6f on Good; Andrew Mullen has a good record of delivering horses from prominent positions and this horse's profile — sitting just off the pace then pouncing — suits the expected race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Overbudget at least posted a third three starts back, though sixth and seventh in more recent outings temper expectations; a trainer firing at just 3% and 42 days off the track are further checks on enthusiasm despite experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Real Jack
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' 3yo is prominent in style and has placed on Good ground, but a 48-day absence is noteworthy and recent form figures of 6-5-6-7-2 suggest consistency is a concern; Connor Beasley is an experienced handler of hold-up and prominent types at Northern tracks, and the 6f trip looks sharper than preferred.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Real Jack does at least bring a second five starts back and handles today's distance and going; our rating of 75 gives him a solid profile edge, and 48 days between runs should leave him fresh stepping off a mark of 62.

runners_data.name: Soul Warrior
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 3yo carries a ⚠ fade flag that is significant in a race where the gallop is likely to be only fair — holds up but is flagged as weakening late, which is a damaging combination when the race may not produce a true end-to-end pace to suit closers; one win and one place from eight runs on Good ground, the Alex Jary (3lb) claim is a small offset.
runners_data.comment: Soul Warrior showed a third two starts back but has been out of the frame more often than not in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 128 lb from stall 11, and an 18-day absence leaves fitness just a shade uncertain.

runners_data.name: Mare Of London
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's 3yo won a claimer at 6f on Good in recent form figures that show a second, and Sam James is a competent jockey for the yard; by nature a come-from-behind horse who will be squeezed forward by the volume of hold-up types in this field, meaning they race in a role that does not suit, and six-from-eight on Good going suggests conditions are not an issue.
runners_data.comment: Mare Of London has been finding the frame difficult of late, but her second **five starts back** shows she can threaten at this level, and distance-and-going experience plus a sharp 14-day turnaround keep her firmly in the mix; the risk is she's been winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Maximum Velocity
runners_data.note: The top-rated horse in the field (OR 65) and Nigel Tinkler's stronger candidate between their two entries; headgear (p - presumably a hood or similar) and a win and four places from 11 runs on Good ground give Faye McManoman solid material, and this hold-up horse is the best-credentialled closer if the pace does genuinely collapse late.
runners_data.comment: Maximum Velocity arrives on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, and he has distance and going experience to call upon here. The chief concern is that his nine starts back showed a tendency to disappoint, and 135 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Yellow Diamonds
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 3yo is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and is expected to dictate, though their form figures of 4-4-4-5-13 show consistency without winning, and the move from 5f to 6f is an unknown; Ryan Sexton's booking for a yard with one win in 17 recent (T14: 1/17) tempers confidence, and the STYLE_FIT flag notes they are arguably running out of their most comfortable role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Yellow Diamonds nonetheless catches the eye with her consistent run of fourth-place finishes — four starts back, three starts back, and two starts back — and she has experience of today's distance and going; at 134 lb from stall 10, the weight could be the sticking point.

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: W H Harrison's 3yo has the best recent form profile of the hold-up runners — three consecutive seconds including two at 6f on Good — and Barry McHugh has ridden with purpose on similar conditions; only 11 days since last run is tight but the horse has been running well, and if any closer gets the right run through in the final furlong, Great Profit is the one with the form to justify it.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Great Profit has finished second in each of his last three starts yet is winless in recent starts, with the eighth four starts back a concern. Suited by today's distance and going, he returns quickly after 11 days and carries 133 lb from stall five.

races.paceDynamic: Yellow Diamonds is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap at Thirsk on Good ground, and with no genuine rival committed to disputing the lead, they should be able to set a measured, sustainable gallop from the off without being pressured into burning excessive early energy. Lope Y Linda, Overbudget, and Real Jack will push up into prominent positions behind, creating a relatively compact and organised early order rather than a chaotic scramble for the front. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses finishing margins and tends to reward horses who can travel smoothly in the first three or four lengths and produce a clean, sharp finish from a handy position — making prominent-to-midfield runners with good Good-ground form the primary beneficiaries. This field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Hellcat, Liquid Cooled, Agric Ranger, and Mare Of London are all true come-from-behind horses who are likely to find themselves racing more prominently than ideal, reducing their ability to produce a trademark late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds slots into an uncontested lead and the hold-up brigade cannot get far enough back to generate a meaningful finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Yellow Diamonds dictates at a fair clip through the first two furlongs and, with no rival willing to run them down early, conserves enough to fight off challengers inside the final furlong; horses travelling prominently off the leader's back get first run on the closers and the race is won close to the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds' lead is modest enough that a prominent tracker travelling strongly makes their move from two furlongs out and catches the front-runner flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A horse like Overbudget or Lope Y Linda, sitting two lengths off the pace with cover, gets a clean passage on the outside and hits the front entering the final furlong; the true hold-up horses, forced too far forward, lack the acceleration to finish past them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds goes too hard early and the pace collapses in the final two furlongs, creating a genuine opportunity for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Maximum Velocity, the highest-rated hold-up type with solid Good-ground form, is best placed to benefit if there is genuine end-to-end pace; Great Profit, with multiple placed efforts on today's conditions, could also pick up the pieces, though both face the reality that hold-up types are compromised by the likely race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace causes a bunched, messy finish with traffic problems throughout the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse who can find clear daylight on the wide outside, irrespective of their drawn position, would benefit most from the resulting sprint finish; this is the least structured outcome and depends heavily on in-running fortune rather than any specific tactical advantage.

watchPoints.text: Yellow Diamonds — if they are challenged for the lead early by Lope Y Linda or Overbudget pushing forward, the resulting fractional increase in pace could be enough to empty the field in the final furlong and fundamentally alter the race shape from the expected controlled scenario.

Maximum Velocity (headgear, p) — watch for how the headgear affects their early behaviour; if they race more keenly than usual, they will not get the patient hold-up trip they need to finish with maximum effect.

Overbudget (42-day absence, 133lbs top weight) — fitness after the break and the weight burden are the two factors to monitor at the start; if they travel sweetly in the first half, they become the most dangerous prominent-type challenger.

Soul Warrior's fade flag — in a moderately-paced 6f on Good ground, any horse who is already flagged as weakening in the finish is a horse to oppose in-running if they are within striking distance two furlongs out; Nigel Tinkler will be aware this is a concern.

Redistribution effect — with Hellcat, Liquid Cooled, Agric Ranger, and Mare Of London all forced closer to the pace than natural, watch for traffic congestion in the final two furlongs as these horses fail to find clear air at the same time, potentially gifting the race to a prominently-placed horse with a clear run.
